title: Collector reading batch, version 1 (draft until the first collector ships)
description: The collector is identified by the token the batch is sent with, never by anything in the batch. A batch with no readings and no missed reads is a heartbeat: a collector with nothing to send sends one, and the answer lists its pending jobs as every answer does.

sent_at.description: The collector's clock when this copy of the batch was sent; a resent batch carries a later time.

clock.description: The collector's clock status when every event in the batch was recorded.

backlog.description: The collector's buffer when the batch was sent, this batch included.

oldest.description: Earliest event timestamp waiting to be sent.

refused.description: Events refused since the collector started, because the buffer was full or a write failed.

quarantined.description: Batches set aside on the collector because the server rejected them permanently.

config.description: The polling config the collector is applying, by its digest (contract/fixtures/config.v1.digests.json), and the served config it refused since, by its digest, with the reason; both null when it has refused none. Optional: a collector that does not fetch its config sends none.

reason.description: Why the refused config was not applied, as the collector's parser gave it.

firmware_reads.description: Meters' software and firmware names. The collector sends a meter's when they, or the serial or product code read with them, differ from the last it sent for that endpoint and unit, and the first after it starts. Optional: a batch with nothing changed has none.

clock_checks.description: The collector's clock measured against an NTP server: at start, once a day, and after a step in its clock. Each check is sent once it ends, answered or not. The four SNTP times are stored as measured, never an offset; offset, delay and error bound are the store's to compute. Ingest keys a check on (collector, t1): a resent check is a duplicate, not a conflict. Optional: a batch sent between checks has none.

latency.description: Each meter's request latency for one UTC date, as one poller counted it: one entry per endpoint, unit, date and poller start, sent once when the date ends by the collector's clock and once when the poller stops, so a restart's part of a day is an entry of its own. Counts, never percentiles: the store computes those. Ingest keys an entry on (collector, endpoint, unit_id, date, poller_started_at): a resent entry is a duplicate, not a conflict. Optional: a batch sent between days has none, and a collector that does not count latency never sends one.

stored_entries.description: Quantities copied from the entries a meter stores (billing histories, daily snapshots, load-survey intervals), one item per quantity per entry. An entry is identified by the meter's own stamp, never by the slot it was read at: ingest keys an item on (meter_serial, store, register_key, meter_time), a resent item is a duplicate, and a different value under a taken key is a conflict, kept beside the first. A quantity the meter reads as NaN is unsupported, as its support mask says, and is not sent. Optional: a batch with no copy in it has none.

meter_clock_reads.description: A meter's own clock, read beside the collector's: at the start and end of each copy visit, and once a day per meter. Raw evidence: an offset is the store's to compute, against the collector's clock checks either side of it. Optional: a batch with no read in it has none.

fill_results.description: One item per meter and store a fill request named, once the collector has copied what the meter holds of the request's range; the entries themselves go in stored_entries, carrying the request_id. Keyed by (request_id, meter_serial, store): a resent item is a duplicate. Optional: a batch with no fill finished in it has none.

config_digest.description: SHA-256 of a polling config's canonical encoding, in lowercase hex (contract/fixtures/config.v1.digests.json).

count.description: At most 2^53 - 1, the largest integer every JSON implementation holds exactly.

profile.description: A profile in contract/profiles, by its name.

profile_version.description: The version of that profile the collector read and decoded under. A version never changes once a batch cites it; a correction is a new version.

request_id.description: The request this was read for, as the server's answer listed it among the collector's jobs. Absent for a read the collector made of its own accord.

decimal.description: A decimal string, never a JSON number, so no float ever carries energy; NaN and infinities are not decimals.

meter_time.description: A meter's clock as the profile version decodes it (meter_clock, or a stored section's stamp): the meter's local time, to the second, with no zone or offset, since the meter keeps none.

meter_serial.description: The serial the meter reported in the round the reading was taken in.

product_code.description: The product code the meter reported in that round, as read.

value.description: The value decoded under the profile version's entry for register_key. Its unit and kind are the entry's. An integer register's value is exact; a float register's is the shortest decimal that names its bits at the register's own width (contract/fixtures/register-decode.v1.json), so the meter's words are recoverable from it.

missed_read.description: A register the collector was due to read and did not.

meter_serial.description: The serial the meter reported in that round, or null when it could not be read. The server keys a missed read on its address, not on this.

timestamp.description: When the read was due and given up on.

reason.description: unreachable: the endpoint could not be connected to; decode: the meter answered with words that do not decode; profile_mismatch: the meter's product code or energy unit setting is not its profile's, or its serial is empty or not printable, so none of its registers were read (see detail); exception: a Modbus exception response (see exception_code); the others are failures of the read itself.

exception_code.description: The Modbus exception code when reason is exception, else null.

detail.description: More about the reason, for people (a socket error, a decode error), or null.

attempts.description: Times the read was tried; 0 when the meter or endpoint was already known to be unreachable.

raw_words.description: What the meter sent when its words did not decode, else null.

name.description: A software or firmware name as decoded under the meter's profile (firmware section), or null when the meter did not give it: it answered blank or with text that is not printable, or with exception 02 (no such register).

firmware_read.description: A meter's software and firmware names, read in a round with its serial and product code.

meter_serial.description: The serial the meter reported in the round the names were read in.

product_code.description: The product code the meter reported in that round, as read.

modbus_version.description: The Modbus protocol version and revision; a hex entry decodes to four uppercase hex digits, such as "0B03".

collector_time.description: The collector's clock, at most microseconds.

server_time.description: The NTP server's clock as its reply gave it, at most nanoseconds (an NTP fraction is 2^-32 s).

clock_check.description: One SNTP query (RFC 4330) and what came of it. answered: a reply the collector accepted, which carries the server's times and the header fields; timeout: no reply in time; unreachable: no query could be sent (the name did not resolve, or the socket failed); kiss_of_death: a reply with stratum 0, which carries the address that sent it and its kiss code in reference_id; invalid: a reply that is not a usable answer (wrong mode, version or originate echo, or a server that says it is unsynchronised). Any other check carries none of the server's fields.

trigger.description: start: the collector started; daily: a day since the last check; step: the collector's clock stepped.

server.description: The NTP server as configured: a name or an address.

t1.description: When the collector sent the query, or tried to.

t4.description: When the collector received the reply, or gave up waiting for one.

t2.description: When the server received the query.

t3.description: When the server sent its reply.

leap.description: The leap indicator: 0 none, 1 a last minute of 61 s, 2 of 59 s. 3 (unsynchronised) makes a check invalid.

reference_id.description: The kiss code (RATE, DENY, RSTR and so on), as the reply carried it.

latency_day.description: One meter's request latency over the part of a UTC date one poller ran. An answer is a sample: a reply with words, or the meter's own exception, timed from send to reply (never the connect). A timeout is censored: counted in timeouts, never a sample; so is exception 0B, the gateway's word that the meter did not answer in time. Anything else (exception 0A, a closed socket, a reply that could not be parsed) is neither. The answers are the sum of buckets.

date.description: The UTC date the requests were made on, by the collector's clock.

poller_started_at.description: When the poller that counted them started, by the collector's clock: before the end of date, and on an earlier date for a poller that ran across midnight.

buckets_version.description: The version of contract/latency's bucket bounds the answers were counted under. A version never changes once a batch cites it.

retries.description: Answers that came on a retry, not the first attempt; at most the answers.

timeouts.description: Requests that timed out, and exception 0B answers.

max_ms.description: The longest answer, exact, in milliseconds; null when nothing answered. It lies in the last bucket that counts any answer.

buckets.description: The answers in each bucket of the version's bounds, in order, every bucket given: one count per bound and one for answers above the last.

ntp_address.description: The address the server's name resolved to, which replied.

reference_id.description: A reply's reference identifier, its 32 bits as an unsigned integer.

stored_entry.description: One quantity of one stored entry, as copied behind the profile version's selector for its store.

meter_serial.description: The serial the meter reported in the visit the entry was copied in.

product_code.description: The product code the meter reported in that visit, as read.

store.description: The profile version's stored section the entry was copied from.

meter_time.description: The entry's stamp: a history's or snapshot's date, a load-survey interval's start.

register_key.description: The quantity, by its key in the store's section of the profile version, which holds its unit and kind.

value.description: The quantity decoded under its entry in the profile version: the shortest decimal that names its bits at the register's own width (contract/fixtures/stored-decode.v1.json).

slot.description: The selector value the entry was read at (a load survey's day selector; its parameter follows from register_key). Evidence only, never part of the entry's identity: a meter's slots shift as it stores new entries.

copied_at.description: When the reply arrived, by the collector's clock.

interval_s.description: The interval's length in seconds, as the meter's interval register gave it; meter_time is its start. Only a load-survey entry has one.

meter_clock_read.description: A read of a meter's clock register, and the collector's clock when the reply arrived.

meter_serial.description: The serial the meter reported in the visit the clock was read in.

profile_version.description: The version whose meter_clock section the time was decoded under.

fill_result.description: A fill request's copy of one meter's store, finished: what of the range the meter no longer held.

meter_serial.description: The serial the meter reported in the visit the fill ran in.

gone_before.description: The requested range's entries stamped before this are no longer on the meter: the stamp of its oldest entry when that falls inside the range, the range's end when the meter holds none of it, or null when the meter holds entries older than the range's start.

finished_at.description: When the copy of this store finished, by the collector's clock.
